technical_validation.duplicate_guard_evidence: r4 checkpoint/rebuild paths reject duplicate ownership; current registry read found one owner per frozen target.
technical_validation.qualification: Mutable global registry was read only for ownership and not hash-locked.

items.evidence: Paragraph 114 summarizes direct adverse effects on affected public servants.
items.scope_review: It supplies no standalone legal impact threshold, damages test or entitlement.

items.evidence: Paragraph 166 quotes the applicant's affidavit about missing manager contact and possible evidentiary consequences.
items.scope_review: The witness complaint is not an adopted universal duty to interview managers or a proof rule; paragraph 167 contains the court's separate assessment.

items.evidence: Paragraph 75 treats selection of the review standard for Commission section 69 jurisdiction/powers as a legal question with no deference to the trial judge.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this addresses appellate treatment of the trial judge, not final selection of correctness versus reasonableness for the Commission. The ultimate jurisdiction issue is later reserved.

items.evidence: Paragraph 101 contrasts a final, nonappealable section 69 decision with a section 67 internal-revocation complaint under section 74 and the Staffing Tribunal route.
items.scope_review: Qualification: nonappealable means no statutory appeal/Staffing Tribunal route described here; it does not eliminate judicial review under the Federal Courts Act.

items.evidence: Paragraph 161 recognizes a legitimate expectation that the matter had ended after finished sworn testimony not directly contradicted in the revised factual report.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this depends on the stated circumstances and evidentiary posture. It is neither immunity nor an absolute rule against reopening an investigation.

items.evidence: Paragraph 59 recounts an unsuccessful report-production request and respondent Rule 317 objections.
items.scope_review: It does not adopt a general record-production threshold; the motion disposition appears separately.

items.evidence: Paragraph 162 reproduces Ms. Cousineau's late e-mail and disputed recollections.
items.scope_review: The quotation is not court adoption of truth, a late-evidence admissibility rule or proof that the applicant knew of false references.

items.evidence: Paragraph 130 makes case-specific credibility and delayed-knowledge findings.
items.scope_review: These are not a reusable fairness rule or an innocence adjudication; paragraph 196 expressly separates procedural relief from innocence.

items.evidence: Paragraph 2 separately states section 29 appointment authority in principle and sections 66-73 broad supervisory jurisdiction over public-service appointments.
items.scope_review: Qualification: historical practical delegation is not part of the first AU; broad supervision does not decide independent third-party sanction power. The primary spans are disjoint.

items.evidence: Paragraph 199 separately excludes non-application former-counsel costs and dismissed-production-motion expenses, then awards $12,000 payable forthwith with a conditional $650 deduction.
items.scope_review: Qualification: the amount is reasonable in this case, not a universal tariff. The $650 is deducted only if not already paid. The two primary spans are adjacent and non-overlapping.

boundaries.note: Only frozen fifteenth10 decisions are accepted; mutable overall progress is outside scope.
